title: A corner of Prairie Avenue
premise: Meet the Glessner House from the street in summer 1904.

opening.text: Begin at Prairie and Eighteenth. This short exterior orientation distinguishes the reconstructed 1904 scene from the later sources used to build it. The route and keepsake are modern interpretation, not a reenacted historical visit.

stops.text: Look across Prairie Avenue toward the Glessner House. The family moved here in December 1887. You are viewing the house in the summer 1904 reconstruction; the street-corner viewpoint is a modern interpretive choice.

From outside, notice the roof and street-facing walls. Glessner’s later account describes unglazed red roof tiles and granite street walls as features of the original construction. That account is evidence about the building, not a record of today’s imagined visit.

endings.text: You have found your bearings at Prairie and Eighteenth. Continue exploring the 1904 scene at your own pace.

keepsake.title: Prairie Avenue bearings
keepsake.text: An interpretive note marking the corner where you began, not a historical artifact.

evidence.text: The family moved into the house in December 1887.
Glessner describes unglazed red roof tiles and granite street walls as part of the house’s construction.
evidence.locator: HABS transcription, data pages 13–15; construction description, not the 1923 garage conversion.
